tagline: The Vapor backend behind Auth — JWT issuance, refresh, and account lifecycle for email, Apple, Google, and guest sign-in.
overview: Auth API is the Vapor server-side of the Auth Swift Package — route collections a host app registers to get email/password, Sign in with Apple, Google Sign-In, and guest authentication with zero hand-rolled JWT or persistence code. It owns the full token lifecycle end to end: JWT generation, non-rotating refresh tokens, guest-to-account upgrade, password reset, and account deletion, all backed by Fluent so the host app only supplies a database driver. The endpoints below are demonstrated end-to-end by the bundled demo/api reference server.
gettingStarted:
## Getting Started

Auth API is the Vapor server-side of the Auth Swift Package. A host app adds Auth as a package dependency, registers each RouteCollection (AuthController, RefreshTokenController, LogoutController, GuestAuthController, UpgradeController, AppleAuthController, GoogleAuthController, ForgotPasswordController, ResetPasswordController, ChangePasswordController, AccountDeletionController) against its Vapor Application, and supplies its own Fluent database driver — Auth itself stays driver-agnostic.

## Authentication

Most endpoints are public: registration, login, refresh, social sign-in, guest sign-in, forgot-password, and reset-password. Endpoints that act on an existing session — logout, guest upgrade, change password, account deletion, and the profile lookup — require a Bearer JWT access token issued by one of the sign-in endpoints, verified by JWTMiddleware.

## Reference server

The endpoints below are demonstrated end-to-end by the bundled demo/api Vapor app, which stores data in SQLite for local development and is started with swift run from demo/api.

endpoints.overview: Registers a new user with an email and password, hashes the password with BCrypt, and returns a fresh access/refresh token pair.

requestFields.description: The new user's email address. Must be unique.
Plaintext password. Hashed with BCrypt before storage.

responseFields.description: ISO 8601 expiry date of the access token.

children.description: The user's email, null for guests.
Always null — not yet settable via this endpoint.

errors.description: A user with this email already exists.

endpoints.overview: Authenticates an existing user by email and password and returns a fresh access/refresh token pair.

requestFields.description: The account's email address.
Plaintext password, verified against the stored BCrypt hash.

responseFields.description: ISO 8601 expiry date of the access token.

children.description: The user's email, null for guests.
The user's display name, if set.
Whether the account is an anonymous guest.

errors.description: The email is not found or the password is wrong.

endpoints.overview: Exchanges a valid, non-expired refresh token for a new access token and a rotated refresh token. Refresh tokens are one-time use — the old one is deleted as soon as a new pair is issued.

requestFields.description: The refresh token previously issued by any sign-in endpoint.

responseFields.description: A fresh signed JWT access token.
A newly rotated refresh token — replaces the one just used.
ISO 8601 expiry date of the new access token.

children.description: The user's email, null for guests.
Whether the account is an anonymous guest.

errors.description: The refresh token was not found or has expired.

endpoints.overview: Invalidates the supplied refresh token, ending the session. Requires a Bearer JWT. Idempotent — a token that is already deleted or never existed still returns HTTP 200 rather than an error.

requestFields.description: The refresh token to invalidate.

errors.description: Missing or invalid Bearer JWT.

endpoints.overview: Creates a new anonymous user tied to a device identifier and returns a fresh access/refresh token pair. Each call creates a distinct guest account — the client is responsible for persisting and reusing the returned tokens rather than calling this repeatedly.

requestFields.description: A stable device identifier generated and persisted by the host app. Recorded but not used for de-duplication.

responseFields.description: Signed JWT access token for the new guest session.
ISO 8601 expiry date of the access token.

children.description: The guest's UUID — the stable identifier for this session.

endpoints.overview: Attaches email/password or social credentials to the authenticated guest session, preserving the guest UUID so no app data is lost. Requires a Bearer JWT for the guest session being upgraded. Supply exactly one credential group: email + password for an email upgrade, or provider + identityToken for a social upgrade.

requestFields.description: The UUID of the guest session to upgrade.
"email", "apple", or "google".
Required for an email upgrade; optional for social upgrades when the provider token doesn't carry one.
Required for an email upgrade; hashed server-side.
Required for apple/google upgrades — the identity token from the provider's SDK.

responseFields.description: Signed JWT access token for the upgraded session.
ISO 8601 expiry date of the access token.
The upgraded user's profile — same UUID as the guest session.

children.description: Same UUID the guest session already had.
Always false after a successful upgrade.

errors.description: Missing/invalid Bearer JWT, or the user was not found.
The account has already been upgraded, or the new email is already taken.
Required fields for the chosen provider are missing.

endpoints.overview: Verifies an Apple identity token (from ASAuthorizationController) and signs the user in, creating an account on first sign-in. Apple only includes the user's email on the very first sign-in for a given app — on repeat sign-ins a stable synthetic address is derived from the token's subject claim so the same Apple ID always maps to the same account.

requestFields.description: Always "apple".
The identity token returned by ASAuthorizationController.

responseFields.description: ISO 8601 expiry date of the access token.

children.description: Real email on first sign-in, otherwise a synthetic @privaterelay.appleid.com address.

errors.description: Apple JWKS is not configured on the server.
The identity token is invalid or tampered.

endpoints.overview: Verifies a Google identity token (from the Google Sign-In SDK) and signs the user in, creating an account on first sign-in.

requestFields.description: Always "google".
The ID token returned by the Google Sign-In SDK.

responseFields.description: ISO 8601 expiry date of the access token.

errors.description: Google JWKS is not configured on the server.
The identity token is invalid or tampered.

endpoints.overview: Initiates a password reset for the given email. Always returns HTTP 200, whether or not the email is registered, to prevent user enumeration. If found, a one-hour reset token is generated and delivered via the host app's injected email transport closure.

requestFields.description: The email address of the account to reset.

errors.description: No email transport closure is configured on the server (fail-fast).

endpoints.overview: Completes a password reset using the one-time token delivered by /auth/forgot-password. The token is invalidated after use.

requestFields.description: The one-time reset token delivered to the user's email.
The new plaintext password. Hashed with BCrypt before storage.

errors.description: The reset token was not found or has expired.

endpoints.overview: Changes the authenticated user's password. Only available to email-authenticated accounts — Apple, Google, and guest accounts have no stored password hash. Requires a Bearer JWT.

requestFields.description: The user's current plaintext password, verified against the stored hash.
The desired new plaintext password. Hashed with BCrypt before storage.

errors.description: Missing/invalid Bearer JWT, or currentPassword does not match the stored hash.
No user with the decoded ID exists.
The account has no stored password (Apple, Google, or guest account).

endpoints.overview: Permanently deletes the authenticated user and every refresh token associated with them. Requires a Bearer JWT. Takes no request body.

errors.description: Missing or invalid Bearer JWT, or the subject claim can't be parsed as a UUID.
No user with the derived ID exists.

endpoints.overview: Returns the authenticated user's profile and current token debug information. Registered by the demo/api reference server (MeController), not by the AuthServer package itself — a host app can mirror this controller or write its own. Requires a Bearer JWT. Takes no request body.

responseFields.description: The user's email address. Empty string for guest users.
ISO 8601 date the account was created.
Whether this is a guest (anonymous) account.
ISO 8601 expiry date of the access token used for this request.
The ID of the active refresh token record for this user.

errors.description: Missing or invalid Authorization header.
The user record or an active refresh token could not be found.
